title: (Senior) Full Stack Engineer (m/f/x) - Based in Germany
description:
Cara Care, a digital health company backed by Bayer AG, is on a mission to improve people’s digestive health through technology. As we expand our product portfolio and modernize our platform, we’re looking for a versatile, pragmatic, and forward-thinking (Senior) Full-Stack Engineer (m/f/x) to help shape the future of digital therapeutics.

Your Role

You’ll join a cross-functional product team with high ownership, lean processes, and a clear focus: deliver real impact to patients. We’re looking for someone who thrives on solving real-world problems with code, is technology-open, and knows when to build fast and when to build right. Your main focus will be building and improving our backend services, while also contributing to our React Native apps. You’ll also help us use AI tools and coding agents thoughtfully in day-to-day engineering, turning emerging capabilities into reliable workflows that improve how we design, build, test, and operate patient-facing products.

Your Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate reliable backend services and APIs, primarily using Python, Django, and PostgreSQL, and contribute targeted changes to our React Native applications with TypeScript.
  • Use AI coding agents to implement features, refactor code, and generate tests. Define clear tasks and constraints, provide relevant context, Provide clear context and constraints, and validate changes through code review, automated tests, and application-level checks.
  • Take an end-to-end view of features: understand how mobile clients, APIs, data models, and infrastructure interact, and make pragmatic technical decisions across these boundaries.
  • Own backend delivery from architecture and implementation to automated testing, deployment, monitoring, and iteration, and continuously improve our CI/CD pipelines.
  • Improve the performance and reliability of our backend services, APIs, and databases.
  • Connect AI-assisted development to engineering and design tools via MCP, for example to automate repetitive coding tasks or check frontend changes against Figma designs. Keep patient data, credentials, and other sensitive information out of unapproved tools and workflows.
  • Collaborate closely with Product, Design, and Medical to explore, define, and deliver patient-centric features across our platform, supporting regulated digital health products for IBS, GERD, and upcoming indications.
  • Uphold technical excellence in architecture, code quality, and security, including applicable requirements under IEC 62304, BSI TR-03161, and the MDR.
  • Mentor other developers and help raise the technical bar across the team.

Requirements

Your Profile

Must haves

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a strong backend focus and an understanding of how complete applications work from user interface to infrastructure.
  • Strong backend development skills in an established language such as Python, TypeScript, Java, or PHP. Our current stack includes Python, Django, and PostgreSQL.
  • Working knowledge of React Native and TypeScript, with the ability to implement and test changes in an existing mobile application.
  • Solid understanding of relational databases, API design, distributed systems and services.
  • Experience writing and maintaining automated tests for backend services and APIs, including unit and integration tests.
  • Solid understanding of backend security and privacy, including authentication, authorization, secrets management, and secure handling of personal and patient data.
  • Strong practical knowledge of containers, Kubernetes, and cloud-native architecture, with experience using GCP or another major cloud provider such as AWS or Azure.
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding agents to implement features, refactor code, and write automated tests, including connecting agents to engineering tools via MCP. You can explain how you scoped the work, verified the results, and handled tool permissions and sensitive data.
  • A pragmatic product mindset: you collaborate effectively with non-technical stakeholders, understand the impact of technical decisions on patients and UX, and continuously improve both product and platform.

Nice-to-have

  • Strong Linux administration skills, including setting up, operating, and securing self-managed cloud instances; familiarity with monitoring and observability concepts.
  • Experience with Prometheus, Loki, and Grafana; GitOps using ArgoCD or FluxCD; or configuration management using Ansible or similar tools.
  • Networking knowledge and experience with mobile CI/CD, release automation, or application monitoring tools such as Sentry.
  • Experience in regulated industries, healthcare, or other security-conscious environments.


💡Please note: Cara Care is a remote-first company with a fully distributed team. All team members are based in Germany so candidates must reside in Germany to join us.

Benefits

💸 Fair compensation: We offer fair pay, regular salary reviews, and the equipment you need to do your best work.

🫶 Great team spirit: Join a vibrant, interdisciplinary team and enjoy a friendly, supportive working atmosphere, with regular in-person team events.

👨‍💻 Remote-first working: Prefer working from home? No problem. Want to join us at our Berlin office? That works too. Our remote-first approach gives you the flexibility to work where it suits you best.

🏝️ 30 days off per year: Rest matters. You’ll get 26 vacation days plus 4 additional company-wide mental health days each year to take a breather and recharge.

🦉 Flexible working hours: Whether you’re an early bird or prefer a later start, you can shape your working day around what works for you.

🏋️ Urban Sports Club (USC): Enjoy access to a wide range of sports, fitness, and wellness activities at discounted rates.

🧠 OpenUp: Access a variety of resources and services to support your mental health and personal wellbeing.

🛍️ Corporate Benefits: Get attractive discounts and exclusive offers from a wide range of well-known brands and providers.

🚀 Make a real impact: Be involved, contribute your ideas, and help shape what comes next. Your voice matters, and you can make a real difference.

About Cara Care

Cara Care is a digital health company on a mission to improve the lives of people with digestive health conditions through holistic, science-based digital therapies.

Our established IBS therapy, Cara Care für Reizdarm, provides personalised content, practical exercises, and symptom tracking to help people better understand and manage their condition. It is listed in the German Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices’ (BfArM) directory of digital health applications (DiGA) and is covered by statutory health insurance in Germany.

We are expanding our product portfolio and evolving our technology platform to bring digital therapies to more people across a broader range of conditions.

Backed by Bayer

We’re proud to share that Cara Care has recently joined the Bayer Group, a move that strengthens our mission and enables us to scale our impact even further. With Bayer’s global healthcare expertise and our innovative digital approach, we’re poised to redefine care for digestive health.

What It’s Like to Work With Us

At Cara Care, you’ll be part of an interdisciplinary team of doctors, designers, engineers, and creatives who are deeply passionate about improving lives. We’re inspired by our patients and driven by real-world impact. We move fast, collaborate closely, and never lose sight of the importance of well-being—both for our users and ourselves.

Diversity Matters to Us

We believe that diverse teams build better products. That’s why we’re committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone—regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, or disability.

We know that applying for a new job is a big step, and we genuinely appreciate your time and effort. We’re excited to get to know you!

title: Staff Backend Engineer, Financial Engineering
description:
About the Team

Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI’s API platform. These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world. We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for. Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.

We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering. These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.

That reach creates challenging engineering problems. We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change. The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.

Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for. The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.

We’re hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience. Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.

  • Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.

  • Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.

  • Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.

  • Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.

  • Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.

  • Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.

  • Scale and evolve live systems while protecting customer access, financial accuracy, performance, and security.

  • Own problems from early design through launch and operation, working with product, design, finance, and other engineering teams to make and test important technical decisions.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with payments, subscriptions, pricing, billing, or other systems that manage customer purchases and revenue.

  • Experience with product catalogs, packaging and bundles, workspace management, entitlements, or usage metering.

  • Experience building financial or transaction systems at scale, checking that records match across systems, or supporting compliance and audits.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

title: Intermediate Backend Engineer, Authorization
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you'll help build and maintain the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. You'll work alongside experienced engineers who guide the larger design decisions, delivering well-scoped changes and growing into ownership of larger parts of the system.

Today, that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every application programming interface (API) request. You'll work on fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and representational state transfer (REST) APIs that enforce them. A single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks, so correctness and performance both matter.

You'll also contribute to moving the permission model to a new authorization stack that pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine. The engine represents access relationships and evaluates permission rules, and can run within the monolith's process or be reached through remote procedure calls using gRPC. You don't need prior Rust experience: several engineers on the team learned it for this work, and we'll support you doing the same.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and the new authorization service
  • Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources, with guidance from senior engineers on the design

What you'll do

  • Implement authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith so permission checks allow intended access and deny unauthorized access.
  • Deliver well-scoped workstreams from feature-flagged rollout through verifying that the old and new systems produce the same results, with review and guidance from senior engineers.
  • Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles so additional resources have permission coverage consistent with the established catalog.
  • Extend and fix authorization enforcement so GraphQL and the REST API enforce the intended permissions consistently.
  • Make incremental refactors to long-lived policy code without changing behavior for existing customers.
  • Investigate and fix reliability, performance, and security issues so affected permission checks return the expected results without regressions.
  • Work with the authentication, platform, and artificial intelligence (AI) teams to document interface contracts that keep permission checks consistent as authorization moves toward a shared service.
  • Contribute to design documents, merge requests, and code reviews so proposed changes have a documented rationale and review feedback is addressed asynchronously.

What you'll bring

  • Solid experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, typically gained over 2 to 4 years or more.
  • Hands-on experience with authorization concepts, such as role-based access control or fine-grained permissions, from work or projects.
  • A security mindset: you treat a permission bug as a security bug and consider who a change could affect before choosing an implementation.
  • Experience making careful changes to existing codebases, including incremental refactors and feature-flagged rollouts that preserve existing behavior.
  • Familiarity with GraphQL or API authorization patterns.
  • Awareness of performance, including how repeated permission checks can add up on every request.
  • Strong written communication and the ability to work effectively when most decisions happen in a document or merge request rather than a meeting.
  • Helpful, but not required: hands-on PostgreSQL experience, or experience with Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture.

We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security.

About the team

We work in a fully asynchronous organization, with most decisions made in documents or merge requests rather than meetings.

GitLab's mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. Our values include collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency. We expect all GitLab team members to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave

Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

Your work will span renewals, overages and reconciliations, subscription visibility, and budget and reservation management, keeping subscription, billing, and account data accurate and reliable. Because these workflows directly affect revenue, customer access, and financial information, you'll use technical judgment, safe and iterative rollouts, and a high bar for reliability and correctness.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Building a clear, reliable subscription view across the Customers Portal and related surfaces
  • Improving manual renewal and auto-renewal flows, including supporting emails, banners, and account experiences

What you'll do

  • Design and build fullstack features across the post-purchase subscription journey.
  • Contribute to the technical design and implementation of new subscription lifecycle capabilities.
  • Partner with Product and Design to translate renewal, billing account, and customer experience requirements into resilient, well-tested solutions.
  • Integrate subscription lifecycle workflows safely with billing, customer account, and internal admin systems.
  • Write maintainable, well-tested code and follow engineering practices for rollout safety and monitoring.
  • Participate in code reviews and provide thoughtful, constructive feedback.
  • Identify and reduce technical debt and architectural risk in the subscription lifecycle.
  • Participate in incident response for subscription and renewal issues, given their potential impact on revenue and customer access.

What you'll bring

  • Professional experience as a fullstack engineer and confidence working across frontend and backend code. Our purchase applications use Ruby on Rails and Vue.js.
  • Experience owning technical direction for a product area, including proposing, discussing, and driving thorough, iterative solutions.
  • Experience building or maintaining transactional or checkout-style flows, ideally in a billing, ecommerce, or subscription context.
  • Familiarity integrating with third-party billing or customer relationship management systems, such as Zuora, Salesforce, or Stripe, is a plus, not a requirement.
  • A focus on safe, incremental delivery given the revenue and customer impact of this work.
  • The ability to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems and propose thorough, iterative solutions.
  • Written and spoken English proficiency sufficient to collaborate in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.
  • Alignment with GitLab's values and a commitment to working in accordance with them.

About the team

The Subscription Lifecycle team is part of GitLab's Monetization section and owns the post-purchase subscription experience. You'll partner with Sales, Finance, Information Technology, and Support on secure, reliable purchasing, billing, provisioning, and utilization workflows, and report to the Engineering Manager, Purchase. The team works asynchronously, with regular planning and retrospectives and shared expectations for deployments, incident management, testing, and rollout safety. GitLab's mission is to enable everyone to contribute and co-create the software that powers our world. The Purchase team's mission is to make it as easy as possible for anyone to buy, add on to, or upgrade GitLab through a single, trustworthy, unified purchase experience. An overview of this role

As an Threat Research Engineer at GitLab, you'll research emerging security threats and turn your findings into protection for GitLab customers. You'll investigate new attack surfaces, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems, and build systems that help detect threats and improve vulnerability advisories.
This is a full-stack role: you'll take an idea from the first research question to a working proof of concept, deploy it, and analyze the results yourself. Artificial intelligence (AI) is central to how we work. You'll use AI tools daily and build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection.

What you'll do
  • Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems.
  • Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools.
  • Analyze software supply chain incidents and events.
  • Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection.
  • Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work.
  • Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories.
  • Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences.
What you'll bring
  • Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with an understanding of package ecosystems and software supply chain attacks.
  • Both a developer mindset and an adversarial mindset: you can build systems and think about how to break them.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI in real work, such as building with large language model (LLM) application programming interfaces (APIs) or agent frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or agent software development kits (SDKs).
  • Strong programming skills in Go or Python, with good software engineering practices, including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and writing maintainable code.
  • Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud.
  • The ability to map attack vectors, explain trade-offs, and use data to move experiments forward, balancing quality, speed, and customer outcomes.
  • Clear writing for engineers and a general audience, and keeping up with security and AI industry trends.
  • Helpful, but not required: Google Cloud Platform (GCP); Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entries or published findings; research on AI agents, LLM applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; blogs, talks, or open source security tools; Terraform or OpenTofu; databases or data pipelines at scale; reverse engineering.
  • You don't need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing (SAST) engines. A high-level understanding is enough.

We're the Threat Research group. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database, which powers GitLab's dependency scanning, and publish our findings on the Security Labs blog.
Our work includes research on the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Serena, a popular MCP coding agent.

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

Airbnb's Online Data organization gives every engineer at Airbnb the power to build real-time data experiences — through simple, intuitive tools, without needing deep database expertise.

Within Online Data, the Storage Foundationteam owns the online serving stores and databases that power Airbnb. We build and operate Airbnb's source-of-truth database: an open-source, distributed NewSQL system running on stateful Kubernetes. It stores critical data — users, listings, and more — and handles over half of all of Airbnb's online OLTP traffic. Our charter: keep this database reliable, secure, scalable, fast, correct, well-tested, and cost-efficient — at Airbnb's scale.

The Community You Will Join

We're hiring two roles within the Database team. Both are described below.

  • Database Performance & Reliability: Dig into the internals of a large-scale, multi-tenant, distributed database — storage, query execution, consensus, change data capture, and shard routing and management. You'll root-cause hard performance, reliability, and stability issues, and partner directly with our open-source database vendor to land fixes upstream.
  • Database Quality & Automation: Build the testing and quality infrastructure that lets us move fast with confidence on an open-source database. You'll bring tools like Jepsen and other database benchmarks into Airbnb's in-house testing stack, drive CI integration with OSS test suites, and design creative solutions for database tiering and representative load shadowing. As AI accelerates development speed and our availability bar climbs toward 99.99%, this role becomes only more critical to how fast and safely we can ship.

  • Build the frameworks and tooling around monitoring, observability, permissions, and service discovery integration.
  • Dig into the query and storage layers to explain latency differences between B-tree and LSM-based storage engines.
  • Design and implement traffic prioritization at the storage layer for connection pooling, CPU prioritization, and reason about traffic
  • Test, validate and safely roll out a new CDC architecture while guaranteeing full transactional correctness across shards.

Your Expertise

  • 5+ years building and operating large-scale, Tier 0 distributed systems.
  • Hands-on experience with database or storage internals: query execution, storage engines, replication, consensus and testing.
  • Ability to own and dive deeply into a complex codebase, ideally an open-source one.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Streaming Infrastructure
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

Airbnb’s Data Infrastructure organization builds the platforms that power data across the company. Within it, the Data Movement & Transformation (DMT) pillar builds the platform that moves data between Airbnb’s storage engines and transforms it along the way.

Today, data moves through many bespoke, one-off pipelines that are built and maintained differently by each team. We’re replacing them with one unified, declarative platform. You define data once, and it is replicated everywhere it needs to go. This work underpins Airbnb’s Data as a Service initiative.

You’ll join the team that owns three connected layers of that platform:

  • Control plane: the layer that turns declarative data definitions into running pipelines, including provisioning, runtime selection, and lifecycle management.
  • Schema: how schemas are defined, tracked, and evolved safely across every system and engine.
  • Realtime Data Infrastructure (RTDI): Kafka and the streaming transport layer that real-time data flows through at scale.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll set technical direction across these layers and stay hands-on in the code.

Examples of the Difference You’ll Make

  • Design and evolve the control plane that automatically provisions Kafka topics, registers schemas, and deploys pipelines from a declarative definition.
  • Build schema management that makes evolution safe and backward compatible across streaming, storage, and warehouse systems.
  • Improve the reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency of RTDI and Kafka at Airbnb’s scale, including capacity, multi-tenancy, and failure handling.
  • Replace fragmented pipeline tooling with shared, self-serve platform abstractions that other teams adopt.
  • Lead design reviews and incident follow-through, and raise the engineering and operational bar for the team.

Your Expertise

  • 9+ years of software engineering, including significant experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, ideally data platforms, event-driven systems, or streaming infrastructure.
  • Hands-on experience with Kafka or a similar distributed log or messaging system, with a good understanding of partitioning, delivery semantics, throughput, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Experience designing schema or data contract systems, such as schema registries, serialization formats like Avro or Protobuf, and compatibility and evolution strategies.
  • Experience building control planes or platform APIs, such as declarative configuration, reconciliation, workflow orchestration, or resource provisioning, ideally on Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with stream processing (e.g., Flink) or change data capture is a plus.
  • A track record of leading ambiguous, multi-quarter projects, taking them from design through delivery in production.
  • Ability to set technical direction, write clear design docs, and align multiple teams, and to mentor and grow other engineers.
  • Experience running large-scale systems in production, including on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

  • Configure, maintain, and enhance Workday modules, including Payroll, Absence, Time Tracking, Benefits and HCM, ensuring systems are reliable and scalable.
  • Partner with People Operations, Compensation, Payroll, and other business teams to gather requirements and translate business needs into effective Workday solutions.

  • Work alongside Payroll to drive US and International payroll configuration, help troubleshoot payroll errors, support ongoing payroll processing

title: Staff+ Software Engineer, Platform Intelligence
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Platform Intelligence turns each new Claude model's abilities into API features that developers can build on. Our goal is to make the full intelligence of each model available through the API. We own the capabilities that shape what Claude can do for developers: tool use, built-in tools such as web search and code execution, thinking controls, structured outputs, and the memory, files, and skills APIs.

We also run the API side of every Claude model launch, including its safety features and controls. That means getting the API ready for each new model, coordinating with research, safeguards, product, and cloud partners, and making sure the model, its features, the SDKs, and the docs all ship together on launch day.

The work sits where research meets product. We work with new models before they are public. When a model gains a new ability, we work out what it should look like as an API, build it, and ship it to developers on our own platform and on cloud platforms. Those decisions shape how developers first use each model. We also own API versioning and the evals that tell us a capability works in production.

What you'll do

You'll lead the design, build, and operation of API capabilities used by developers around the world. You'll work with research to understand what a new model can do and turn that into an interface that is simple, durable, and hard to misuse.

About the Role

Cloudflare’s architecture is built on a homogeneous edge: every server in over 330 cities runs every service—from L4/L7 proxies (FL2, Pingora) and DNS to the Workers runtime, cache, and storage. While this design maximizes hardware utilization, it creates a difficult distributed attribution problem. Machine-level telemetry tells us how loaded a server is, but not which product, customer, or upstream service is responsible for that load.


MAPS (Metrics and Analytics for Product Segmentation) is a newly formed team building the core instrumentation, collection, and data platform to solve this from the ground up. We are architecting a system to continuously measure CPU, network bandwidth, memory, and storage utilization across the entire global fleet without sampling—attributing resource consumption both to the underlying system service and to the specific product, account, and zone being served.


The data MAPS produces serves two critical functions at Cloudflare:

  1. Real-Time Control Plane: MAPS is the primary telemetry input for Cloudflare’s next-generation global load balancer, shifting traffic management from open-loop heuristics to closed-loop routing driven by real-time, per-service resource capacity and consumption (within seconds).
  2. Fleet Economics & Capacity Planning: MAPS provides the long-term analytical dataset in ClickHouse used to map product demand forecasts to physical hardware requirements, calculate true cost-to-serve per product, and drive multi-year infrastructure investments.

What You’ll Do

You will work across the full lifecycle of a greenfield, high-throughput telemetry system running on every machine at the Cloudflare edge:

  • Host-Level Instrumentation ("Outside View"): Build and maintain low-overhead Linux daemons (netacctd, maps_collector) in Rust and C that use eBPF (cgroup_skb) and cgroup v2 accounting to measure per-service resource consumption directly from the kernel.
  • High-Performance Client Libraries ("Inside View"): Architect non-blocking, zero-allocation reporting SDKs in Rust and Go used by Cloudflare’s highest-throughput data-plane services to report per-request resource usage and product attribution over local Unix domain sockets.
  • Edge Aggregation & Streaming: Build the per-machine collector daemon that ingests millions of events per second, performs bounded in-memory time-window aggregation, serves low-latency gRPC streams to the global load balancer, and flushes batch rollups to ClickHouse.
  • Reconciliation & Correctness: Solve complex attribution problems—such as reconciling kernel-level cgroup measurements against application-reported metrics, and attributing resource usage when one multi-tenant service executes work on behalf of another.
  • Cross-Team Architecture: Partner directly with the engineering teams behind Cloudflare’s core proxies, runtimes, and storage engines to instrument their critical paths without degrading tail latency.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong systems programming experience in Rust, Go, or C, with a solid grasp of memory layout, concurrency, and performance-critical code paths.
  • Experience designing and operating latency- and resource-sensitive server infrastructure or high-throughput data pipelines at scale.
  • Strong fundamentals in Linux systems internals—processes, cgroups, sockets, and how the kernel accounts for compute, memory, and I/O.
  • Proven ability to work across organizational boundaries: reading unfamiliar codebases, aligning with other infrastructure teams, and driving complex integrations to completion.
  • A pragmatic approach to owning outcomes—from kernel-level data collection and wire protocols (protobuf/Cap'n Proto) all the way to the analytical tables consumers query.

Bonus Points

  • Hands-on experience writing and verifying eBPF programs, or deep familiarity with the Linux networking stack and scheduler.
  • Experience designing schemas and query patterns for distributed columnar databases (particularly ClickHouse) at high ingestion rates.
  • Background in profiling, benchmarking, and debugging performance bottlenecks in production Linux environments (perf, PMU counters, flamegraphs).

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Software Engineer on GitLab’s Vulnerability Management team, you’ll help build the core security workflows that GitLab Ultimate customers use to triage, prioritize, and act on vulnerabilities. You’ll work primarily in Ruby on Rails on backend systems, including security dashboards, vulnerability reports, and ingestion pipelines. You’ll take ownership of well-defined projects, solve technical problems with support from experienced team members, and collaborate with other engineers. You’ll also have opportunities to contribute beyond the backend when the work requires it.

You will join a fullstack team, working together with product managers, designers, and frontend engineers to solve problems across the Vulnerability Management domain.

What you’ll do

  • Develop and maintain backend features for GitLab’s vulnerability management workflows.

  • Confidently ship features and improvements with minimal guidance and support from other team members; collaborate with the team on larger projects.

  • Help improve the performance, reliability, and scalability of security data ingestion and reporting systems.

  • Collaborate with frontend engineers and contribute across the stack when needed.

  • Work with engineers across security teams as vulnerability data and workflows come together in Vulnerability Management.

  • Collaborate with Product Management and Product Design to maintain a high bar for quality

  • Craft code that meets our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices for a high-scale web environment

  • Conduct code reviews within our Code Review Guidelines and ensure community contributions receive a swift response

  • Recognize impediments to our efficiency as a team ("technical debt"), propose and implement solutions

  • Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience building and maintaining backend applications with Ruby on Rails.

  • Experience delivering and maintaining software systems as part of a larger engineering team.

  • The ability to investigate technical problems, ask for context when needed, and work toward a practical resolution.

  • Experience working with relational databases such as PostgreSQL.

  • Clear communication and collaboration skills in a distributed team.

  • An interest in learning from others, sharing knowledge, and growing your technical skills.

  • Frontend development experience, including JavaScript or Vue.js, is helpful.

  • Experience with Elasticsearch, graph databases, vulnerability management, application security, or related transferable skills is helpful.

About the team

The Vulnerability Management team develops the core security workflows that help GitLab customers triage and manage vulnerabilities. The team owns areas including the security dashboard, vulnerability reports, and ingestion pipelines, and serves as an important interface for security-related features across GitLab. The team is focused on moving beyond lists of findings toward workflows that help customers prioritize and coordinate remediation. You’ll collaborate asynchronously with a small, distributed group and with related security teams, including the Agentic Security Flows team.

  • Flexible Paid Time Off

About the role

As a Staff Backend Engineer, you will provide technical leadership across your team and adjacent teams, solving the highest-scope and most complex problems in your area. You will lead large, cross-cutting backend initiatives, drive our modular architecture strategy, and define the standards that let teams move faster without compromising quality, security, reliability, or operability.

This is a technical leadership role that combines deep backend expertise, systems judgment, product judgment, and influence across organizational boundaries. You will work with Product, Frontend, Infrastructure, Security, Data, Engineering Managers, and engineers across product groups, bringing subject matter expertise, and you will do it without relying on formal authority.

Why you’ll love this role

  • Leverage: Your work multiplies across teams. The platforms, standards, and architectural decisions you lead determine how quickly everyone else can ship.
  • Genuinely Hard Problems: You’ll lead the modernization of a large monolith toward modular, reusable, appropriately independent systems — at the scale of a platform used by millions of users.
  • Influence Without Bureaucracy: You’ll shape technical direction across teams through clear written proposals and decision records, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform roadmap and investment trade-offs.
  • Frontier AI Work: You’ll lead adoption of AI-assisted and agentic engineering workflows and define the review, quality, security, and privacy guardrails that make them safe to rely on.
  • Autonomy: You’ll thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.

What you’ll do

  • Lead Cross-Cutting Initiatives: Lead the technical design and delivery of large backend initiatives that span teams, and identify and remove systemic bottlenecks across product and infrastructure groups.
  • Own Architecture Strategy: Drive modular backend, service, data, and platform architecture. Lead modernization of the monolith and legacy backends toward modular, reusable, and appropriately independently operated systems — while preventing fragmentation and service sprawl.
  • Set the Standards: Define and improve standards for APIs, contracts, compatibility, schema evolution, testing, security, performance, observability, operability, and maintainability — plus the build, test, deploy, release, rollback, and production-readiness practices needed to operate modular features safely.
  • Establish Shared Patterns: Create the patterns for dependency management, data ownership, eventing, failure isolation, service maturity, and operational documentation. Establish Go service patterns and Kubernetes operating practices where they matter to our production estate, and guide Rust adoption where it solves a real systems, security, performance, or supply-chain problem.
  • Own What You Build in Production: Take part in on-call and incident response for the systems your teams own, act as a technical escalation point during complex incidents, and turn what you learn into architectural and operational improvements that prevent recurrence.
  • Influence and Partner: Shape technical direction across teams without formal authority, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform-level roadmap decisions and investment trade-offs.
  • Grow Engineers: Mentor Senior and Intermediate engineers, shepherd technical debt reduction and reusable patterns that improve throughput, and raise the technical capability of the wider team.
  • Lead AI Adoption: Lead team-level adoption of AI-assisted and agentic workflows, including the quality, security, privacy, and operational guardrails, and help engineers direct, validate, reject, and course-correct agent output.

What you’ll bring

  • Cross-Team Technical Leadership: A sustained record of technical leadership across more than one team or a broad product area.
  • Deep Architecture Experience: Deep backend architecture and production experience in complex applications, services, or platforms, including scaling or governing APIs, service platforms, data systems, modular monoliths, or shared backend components.
  • Modularization in Production: Experience modernizing a monolith or legacy backend architecture in production, and with modular architecture such as bounded contexts, package encapsulation, ports and adapters, service extraction, event-driven boundaries, or an equivalent approach.
  • Influence Without Authority: A strong ability to create alignment through clear written proposals and decision records, so decisions are documented, understood, and adopted without constant escalation.
  • Product Judgment: The ability to balance customer outcomes, delivery speed, technical health, reliability, and long-term platform investment.
  • Mentorship: Experience mentoring engineers and shaping standards through code review, documentation, and example.
  • Agentic AI Leadership: Production experience with AI-assisted or agentic engineering workflows, including the ability to evaluate and improve how a team adopts them.

Helpful experience

  • Go services and APIs at scale.
  • Kubernetes and cloud-native operations, including deployment, scaling, observability, rollback, and production readiness.
  • Rust adoption or production ownership for systems, security, performance, or platform components.
  • Ruby/Rails modularization and large-monolith modernization.
  • PostgreSQL scaling, data partitioning, queues, messaging, or distributed systems.
  • Security-sensitive product or software supply chain engineering.

description:

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll help lead two important areas for GitLab Security: the data layer behind our vulnerability and dependency management capabilities, and our move toward services outside the GitLab monolith. You'll design and develop systems that ingest, store, index, and query security report data, including integrations with key third-party systems. With a strong focus on PostgreSQL and scalable backend design, your work will support security features delivered by teams across GitLab.

You'll take ownership of large deliverables from early ideas through implementation, working directly with product, design, frontend, and engineering partners to shape the technical and product roadmap. You'll stay hands-on across GitLab's Ruby on Rails application and newer services, including greenfield projects, while helping the team build its expertise in modular service design.

What you’ll do

  • Lead large technical deliverables from initial problem definition through delivery, often across multiple months or quarters.
  • Design and develop backend systems for vulnerability and dependency management, including security report ingestion, storage, indexing, querying, and integrations with key third-party systems.
  • Build and improve systems using Ruby on Rails and PostgreSQL, and contribute to newer services using technologies such as Go or Rust where appropriate.
  • Shape technical plans, break down complex work, and help other engineers deliver effectively.
  • Work directly with product, design, frontend, and engineering partners to make clear decisions, resolve constraints, and deliver measurable progress.
  • Influence the team's product and technical roadmap through hands-on investigation, clear proposals, and iterative delivery that demonstrates progress in each monthly release cycle.
  • Apply a security mindset when designing systems, including considering how GitLab identifies and handles malicious or vulnerable software packages.
  • Define patterns for modular services, provide technical leadership when vulnerability management work spans multiple GitLab areas, and share that expertise across GitLab Security.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience leading complex backend projects from idea through delivery while remaining hands-on with design and development.
  • Strong PostgreSQL experience, including evidence of query optimization, table optimization, and write-ahead log management in data-intensive systems.
  • Strong professional experience with Ruby on Rails or Go and comfort working in Ruby on Rails day to day. Experience with large monoliths is helpful, along with an interest in working across languages and services.
  • Experience shaping delivery plans, guiding technical decisions, and supporting the work of other engineers.
  • The ability to collaborate with a range of partners and explain technical trade-offs clearly.
  • Experience communicating with leaders, leading peers through complex delivery, identifying constraints, and moving work forward.
  • Experience using security tooling for activities such as vulnerability triage and remediation, or professional experience building vulnerability management, dependency management, or related security products.
  • Experience with large-scale data systems or established software products. We welcome transferable experience from outside the security domain.
  • Fluency in using artificial intelligence tools to improve delivery while applying sound engineering judgment.

About the team

The Vulnerability Management team contributes to GitLab's move toward modular services and will help other Security teams adopt these patterns over time. Today, we include two Staff Software Engineers, two Senior Software Engineers, and one Intermediate Software Engineer across the United Kingdom, Poland, the Netherlands, and India. You'll work closely with us, product partners, and engineering leaders across GitLab.

We work with clear goals and shared priorities. You'll receive clear context and outcomes, then have the space to own delivery, communicate decisions and progress, ask for help early, and work directly with the partners needed to get the job done.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave

Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

Our mission at Marketing Technology is to provide a state-of-the-art platform and measurement capabilities to enable marketing and product teams to engage with our customers effectively. Every day, millions of Airbnb customers are reached via our streamlined platform over comprehensive marketing channels such as Email, Push, SMS, Google Ads, and Facebook Ads. We deliver substantial business impact by enabling numerous stakeholders across the company, including Marketing (Brand and Performance), Guest, Host, Airbnb Org, Policy, and more.

The Difference You Will Make:

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Segmentation & Insights Platform team, you’ll lead projects end-to-end and help shape how Airbnb reaches its guests and hosts. Our team builds the high-scale backend systems that segment guests, hosts, and other entities. These systems handle 100k+ requests per second and power marketing, in-app experiences, and many other use cases across Airbnb. We’re also building the agentic workflows behind the future of Marketing Technology and Airbnb’s autonomous Growth Engine. You’ll take on ambiguous problems across both areas, driving them independently from design through launch.

A Typical Day:

  • Scale the core platform so it stays highly available, low-latency, and observable. You’ll debug hard problems, find bottlenecks, and optimize systems to keep up with growing demand.
  • Build agentic features for Airbnb's autonomous Marketing Growth Engine, contributing primarily to campaign ideation and refinement.
  • Lead projects across the full development lifecycle: technical design, implementation, testing, experimentation, and production rollout.

  • Take part in on-call rotations, incident response, and post-mortems to keep systems that serve millions of guests and hosts reliable.
  • Use AI tools to work efficiently and run multiple workstreams in parallel, while still owning the quality, correctness, and long-term health of everything you ship.

description:

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The world is changing how it works; not just in where we do it, but in how fast and how well we can do it. Airbnb has already shown that we can move with speed and intention. We navigated a pandemic, rebuilt our company from the ground up, had a successful IPO, and shipped product upgrades – all while working remotely. That experience didn't just change where we work. It changed what we believe is possible.

Now, a new shift is underway. AI is fundamentally changing the leverage available to every team – compressing timelines, breaking down traditional job description silos, raising the ceiling on quality, and enabling small, focused groups to accomplish what once required much larger ones. At Airbnb, we are not treating AI as a future consideration. We are moving fast to embed it into how we operate today – using it to multiply the impact of every employee, every system, and decisions we make every day. The companies and teams that embrace this shift with urgency and discipline will define what's possible in the years ahead. We intend to be one of them.

Collaboration Products

The Collaboration Products team owns the enterprise systems that Airbnb's workforce relies on to plan, build, and deliver — including our Atlassian ecosystem, AI-powered tooling integrations, and custom-built engineering platforms. Our mission goes beyond keeping the lights on. We are moving fast to modernize our stack, retire technical debt, and integrate AI capabilities that directly multiply the productivity and quality of the teams we serve. We build with urgency, operate with rigor, and treat every system we touch as an opportunity to raise the bar on what BizTech delivers to Airbnb.

The Difference You Will Make:

The Senior Systems Engineer is a hands-on technical leader who moves fast, builds to last, and uses AI as a force multiplier — not a future initiative. In this role, you will own the configuration, migration, and continuous improvement of Airbnb's Atlassian platforms, including leading the active deprecation of Jira Data Center and full transition to Jira Cloud. But your impact goes beyond administration. You will identify where AI and automation can compress delivery cycles, reduce toil, and improve the quality and reliability of the systems our workforce depends on — and then build those improvements, quickly. You bring the platform depth to architect scalable solutions and the judgment to know when to move fast and when to be deliberate. You are the kind of engineer who raises the velocity and quality of everyone around you.

A Typical Day:

  • Serve as the primary SME and hands-on administrator for JiraCloud Software, JiraCloud Service Management (JSM), and associated Atlassian tooling; own configuration standards, governance, and technical debt reduction across the environment
  • Architect and implement scalable Jira configurations including custom workflows, issue type hierarchies, permission schemes, notification schemes, screens, and field configurations aligned with Atlassian best practices
  • Lead and execute Jira migrations - including Data Center to Cloud - coordinating with cross-functional stakeholders to deliver seamless cutover experiences
  • Design and configure Jira Service Management projects including SLAs, custom queues, JSM Forms, approval workflows, and security schemes to support internal service delivery teams
  • Build and maintain advanced analytics, dashboards, and reporting solutions using native tooling for Jira Cloud as a first line of options; Airbnb has elected to avoid Atlassian Marketplace products for information security, privacy & legal prerogatives. Airbnb is building custom Forge applications that will require your ongoing maintenance and partnership with supporting systems engineering teams.
  • Configure and administer Atlassian access management, user lifecycle management, license tier optimization, and security posture improvements
  • Evaluate if Atlassian Marketplace plugins architecture evolves to a point where Airbnb could consider adopting plugins where business needs dictate, and where security, legal, and privacy requirements are satisfied.
  • Act as a strategic partner to business stakeholders by leading requirements-gathering sessions, translating business needs into technical designs, and proactively identifying opportunities for automation and process improvement
  • Configure and expand Atlassian Rovo AI agents and automation rules; evaluate emerging AI/ML capabilities within the Atlassian ecosystem and champion responsible, contextually appropriate AI adoption aligned with Airbnb's mission
  • Write and maintain custom automation rules using Jira's native Automation engine and JavaScript; leverage Jira REST API for integrations, data imports, and custom reporting
  • Lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) efforts for platform changes and migrations; develop and maintain test plans, test scripts, and defect tracking documentation
  • Facilitate Agile ceremonies (sprint planning, retrospectives, standups) as needed; operate as Scrum Master or Product Owner for platform-focused workstreams
  • Document system configurations, runbooks, and knowledge base articles to support operational continuity and enable self-service across the organization
  • Participate in on-call rotation and provide escalation support for critical Atlassian platform issues


Your Expertise:

  • 7+ years of hands-on Atlassian administration experience, including Jira Software, Jira Service Management (across JiraCloud & JiraDC) in enterprise environments with large user populations
  • Deep expertise in Jira workflow design, including post functions, validators, conditions, and custom properties; strong command of JQL for filters, subscriptions, dashboards, and board configuration
  • Proven experience leading Jira migrations (Data Center to Cloud), including project configuration migration, macro compatibility, and data integrity validation
  • Experience configuring and administering Jira Cloud native tooling for capacity planning and portfolio reporting
  • Proficiency with Atlassian Marketplace plugins including JavaScripting
  • Hands-on experience with Jira REST API using tools like Postman (GET/PUT/POST) for data extraction, integration, and custom reporting workflows
  • Experience integrating Atlassian tools with identity providers via LDAP & Okta; familiarity with user lifecycle management, license governance, and security hardening practices
  • Working knowledge of Atlassian Rovo and AI/ML capabilities within the Atlassian ecosystem; ability to configure Rovo agents with careful consideration for AI ethics, value alignment, and contextual appropriateness
  • Experience configuring Jira Automation rules (native and scripting-based); working knowledge of JavaScripting and JSON for custom automation
  • Strong background in Jira Service Management including SLA configuration, JSM Forms, custom queues, and approval workflows
  • Experience leading UAT for complex migrations and platform changes; proficiency in developing and executing test plans, test scripts, and defect documentation
  • Familiarity with SAFe Agile (SAFe Agilist and/or SAFe Scrum Master certification a plus); experience as Scrum Master or Product Owner for technical workstreams
  • Strong analytical and communication skills with a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience working in a remote-first, high-growth environment; ability to independently manage multiple priorities and keep stakeholders informed
  • Familiarity with complementary enterprise tools such as Slack, Asana, Figma, Airtable, and Miro is an advantage

title: Staff Software Engineer, Tech Foundations
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

Airbnb's mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. Our community of guests and hosts rely on Airbnb around the clock to facilitate millions of stays and experiences per day.

The Observability team builds the platform Airbnb engineers use to understand how their systems behave in production. We collect, process, store, and query metrics, logs, events, and traces from both backend services and client apps. Our metrics platform alone ingests tens of millions of samples per second across more than a billion active time series. AI agents are now consumers of this data alongside engineers: they query telemetry to write and validate code and to help debug production issues. We continue to invest in reliable and efficient real time system for both AI and human access.

The Difference You Will Make:

As a Staff engineer, you will set the technical direction for a major area of the Observability platform and lead it from design through production. Problems in front of us include:

  • Scaling the metrics pipeline (OpenTelemetry, vmagent, Grafana Mimir) while controlling cost through aggregation, sampling, and blocking unused metrics.
  • Replacing legacy log aggregation with an OpenTelemetry-based pipeline, and evolving log and trace storage on OpenSearch.
  • Building a fast, reliable query layer for both engineers and AI agents, with rate limiting, access control, isolation, and caching so agent traffic does not slow down incident response.
  • Giving teams self-service visibility and control over their telemetry cost: unit cost per team and service, and controls for granularity, sampling, and retention.
  • Improving time to detect with anomaly detection and automated correlation across signals.

A Typical Day:

  • Lead the design and delivery of distributed systems that handle tens of millions of events per second, from prototype to production operation.
  • Write well-crafted, well-tested, readable, maintainable code, and contribute back to the open-source projects we run on.
  • Align roadmaps across Observability and partner infrastructure and product teams, and drive build, buy, and open-source decisions.
  • Explain tradeoffs and return on investment to engineering leadership in terms of reliability, cost, and developer productivity.
  • Mentor engineers on the team and raise the bar on design reviews, operational readiness, and on-call.
  • Help Airbnb engineers instrument their services and self-serve when debugging production issues.

Your Expertise:

  • 9+ years of industry experience, with a track record of building and operating large-scale distributed systems in production.
  • Led the technical direction of a system or multi-team project end to end: wrote the design, aligned stakeholders, delivered it, and operated it.
  • Deep experience in at least one telemetry domain at scale: metrics (Prometheus, Grafana Mimir, VictoriaMetrics), logs (OpenSearch, Kafka), or distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, ClickHouse).
  • Strong coding skills in Go or Java/Kotlin, and comfortable working in unfamiliar codebases, including upstream open source.
  • Experience with cloud-native infrastructure: Kubernetes, AWS, and service mesh (Istio, Envoy).
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including design docs and tradeoff analysis for engineering leadership.

Nice to Have:

  • Contributions to OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana Mimir, VictoriaMetrics, OpenSearch, Jaeger, or similar projects.
  • Experience with time series storage internals, high-cardinality data, or query performance.
  • Anomaly detection, automated correlation, or SLO-based alerting.
  • Telemetry cost attribution or cost optimization at scale.
  • Building APIs or tools for AI agents that consume operational data, such as MCP servers.
  • Columnar analytics stores such as ClickHouse.

title: Data Center Design Engineer

We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. What you'll do:

  • Work cross-functionally with Cloudflare data center engineering team and other internal teams (capacity planning, network strategy, security) to verify scope and solution and create repeatable standard installation procedures
  • Take ownership of and lead projects to design and implement data center expansions or new data centers on tight deadlines with minimal oversight
  • Technical support in negotiations with external data center partners
  • Assist in RFP preparation, review and cost/engineering analysis
  • Review one-line diagrams and cooling equations for new and existing data centers (Data Center M&E)
  • Power component (PDU) review/approval for Hardware sourcing team
  • Implement, document and maintain power consumption tracking tools and fulfil ad-hoc reporting requests
  • Research new and innovative power efficiency technologies and programs
  • Travel up to 25% to perform infrastructure audits, validate data center construction work and buildouts, and participate in commercial processes.
  • Develop and execute modular and prefabricated data center construction strategies to accelerate time-to-market and optimize cost efficiency
  • Perform electrical short-circuit, coordination, arc flash, and load flow engineering studies to ensure system reliability and compliance
  • Other duties as assigned
  • Partner with Hardware Sourcing and SRE/Infrastructure teams to validate PDU specifications, rack integration plans, and power distribution topologies across global PoP footprints
  • Lead electrical design and end-to-end execution for new sites, expansions, and infrastructure upgrades from site qualification and basis of design through energization, commissioning, and operational handover
  • Serve as Cloudflare's electrical owner's representative, defining design criteria, scopes, deliverables, responsibility matrices, review gates, and acceptance requirements for data center operators, consulting engineers, contractors, commissioning agents, utilities, and vendors
  • Design and review utility-to-rack infrastructure, including utility service, transformers, switchgear, generators, UPS systems, transfer systems, modular and prefabricated electrical assemblies, busway, feeders, whips, rack PDUs, grounding, and metering
  • Define electrical interfaces and auxiliary-load requirements for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, coolant distribution units (CDUs), pumps, controls, leak detection, facility water systems, and heat-rejection equipment
  • Develop and review basis-of-design documents, single-line diagrams, specifications, equipment schedules, calculations, sequences of operation, and interface control documents
  • Oversee technical acceptance of FAT, SAT, Level 1–5 staged commissioning, integrated systems testing, failure-mode testing, deficiency closure, and turnover documentation
  • Define EPMS, metering, telemetry, and capacity-tracking requirements for operational power and capacity management

Requirements

  • Bachelors or equivalent experience plus 5+ years of experience in data center mechanical and electrical design and operations/deployment/installation, P.E. certification or equivalent a plus
  • Experience in HVAC, Chilled Water Systems, Condenser Water Systems, Pump controls, Glycool/Glycols, AHU units (DX, split, RTU, CRAC, etc.), CRAH, Raised Floor Systems, HOT/COLD aisle containment and Building Management Systems
  • Understanding of basic electrical theory (voltage, current, power), basic circuit design & analysis, and single- and three-phase power systems
  • Familiarity with Data Center M&E infrastructure design concepts, electrical/UPS topologies, cooling methodologies (central plant, room cooling, high density thermal strategies)
  • Familiarity with industry standards for resilient Data Center design and Uptime Institute Tier Classifications
  • Excellent verbal, written communication and presentation skills
  • Experience working with multiple time zones and multiple cross-functional teams
  • Experience working on time sensitive projects with delivery responsibility under pressure
  • Understanding of network hardware architecture, data center switching/routing infrastructure, and optical line/transceiver power and thermal profiles
  • Experience acting as an owner's technical representative, governing external delivery partners, reviewing third-party designs, resolving technical disputes, and driving noncompliance and project risks through documented closure
  • Expertise in medium- and low-voltage distribution, transformers, generators, UPS systems, switchgear, transfer systems, busway, grounding, protection, and rack-level power architectures for high-density deployments
  • Understanding of direct-to-chip liquid cooling and the electrical dependencies of CDUs, pumps, controls, facility water systems, and heat-rejection equipment
  • Experience with construction administration, equipment testing, energization planning, staged commissioning, integrated systems testing, deficiency management, and failure-mode testing
  • Experience with utility coordination, design-deviation governance, power-quality or incident investigations, and lifecycle management of mission-critical electrical infrastructure

Bonus Points

  • Degree in electrical/mechanical engineering or IT a plus
  • Experience in large-scale mission critical facility infrastructure design, construction, commissioning, and/or operations a plus
  • Experience with industry standards and building codes including NFPA 70/NEC, IEEE, NEMA, ANSI, UMC, ASHRAE, UBC, LEED, and Uptime Institute standards
  • Knowledge of programming languages a plus
  • JIRA, Confluence admin-level experience a plus
  • AutoCAD experience a plus
  • Experience with FLOTHERM or Tileflow a plus
  • Hands-on experience with hardware validation, power/cooling capacity modeling, or thermal simulation tools (such as FLOTHERM or Tileflow)
  • Familiarity with systems programming, scripting (Python, Go, or Bash), or automation workflows for power/infrastructure tracking
  • Experience with NVIDIA DGX, GB200/GB300 NVL, OCP Open Rack, or comparable liquid-cooled GPU platforms and AI factory reference architectures
  • Experience with ETAP, SKM PowerTools, EasyPower, or equivalent software for dynamic modeling, generator transient analysis, harmonic analysis, and UPS compatibility assessment

Experience with EPMS/BMS integration, branch-circuit monitoring, rack-level telemetry, metering, capacity forecasting, or automated infrastructure reporting

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.
